subject: Temporary capacity bridge for evaluation workload — request & ops plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara@horizon-ai.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary capacity bridge for Horizon evaluation (2-week window)

Team — looping you in on a request from Horizon. They want to run a two-week, high-concurrency eval to compare a set of open models vs their in-house model. Their ramp profile is spiky (short bursts at 20–30k concurrent tokens for 30–90s each). They asked whether we can provide a temporary reserved "bridge" (dedicated slice + autoscale exception) to prevent throttling and reduce tail latency for the eval period.

High-level ask from Horizon (Sara CC'd):
- Reserve a 10-GPU slice (A10g-equivalent) for 14 days starting 2028-06-10
- Allow autoscale headroom up to +40% above the slice for short bursts (policy exception)
- Provide token-level cost estimates and a credit for any SLA deviations during the test window

What I need from you:
- Kimberly: pricing/credit pathway for short-term reserved slices and SLA exception language we can offer quickly (legal looped if needed)
- Marcus & Dev: ops feasibility — can we put an autoscale exception with a strict timebox and hard rollback? Can we enable prefix caching for the eval to reduce token spend? Please include telemetry hooks so we can track cost vs baseline.
- Laura: product ask — any recommended model variants or parallelization knobs we should surface to the customer to make their tests reproducible (and to avoid noisy neighbor issues)

I've attached Horizon's load plan (horizon-eval-loadplan.xlsx) and a quick draft runbook (bridge-ops-runbook.md). Sara — adding you so we stay aligned on start dates.

Karthik
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara@horizon-ai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity bridge for Horizon evaluation (2-week window)

Thanks Karthik — quick notes from pricing/legal side. We can support a short-term reserved slice with an "evaluation surcharge" rate. For SLA exceptions/credits, we need:
- A clear start/end timestamp and a single point of contact for incident escalation.
- Language limiting credit to measurable SLO misses (p50/p95/p99 latency for generation endpoints) — we can use the template in sla-exemption-template.pdf (attached) and iterate.

Two questions before I sign off to legal:
1) Do we anticipate any persistent risk to other Dedicated customers (noisy neighbor)? If so, Marcus please propose isolation knobs (networking, CP scheduling) and whether eviction preemption is acceptable.
2) Billing model — do we bill at reserved slice rate + overage per-burst, or do we precompute a flat credit-backed cost for the window? I prefer the latter for Horizon as it simplifies procurement.

If legal is needed I'll pull them in, but given this is a 2-week ephemeral agreement I'd rather keep it scoped.

Kimberly
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara@horizon-ai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity bridge for Horizon evaluation (2-week window)

Folks — ops feasibility check and proposed guardrails. TL;DR: feasible with two short-lived config changes + monitoring; recommend a 14-day timebox + hard auto-revert. Details and steps below.

What we'll do (technical plan):
- Create a temporary reserved slice (10 GPUs) on the Dedicated pool tied to Horizon's org id. Slice will be isolated at the cgroup-level and have isolated NVMe prefetch so we limit noisy neighbor impact.
- Autoscale exception: allow burst headroom up to +40% for up to 120s per event, with a global cap of X bursts per hour (we'll enforce via rate-limiter). Implementation: a policy flag on the routing layer that bypasses soft-threshold throttles for tagged requests and logs bursts in telemetry.
- Telemetry: add per-request tags (horizon_eval:true) and expose a dashboard with p50/p95/p99 latency, token consumption, and concurrency. We'll also enable prefix/KV caching for the experiment model IDs to reduce repeated compute.
- Rollback and safety: automatic rollback at 2028-06-24T00:00:00Z; ops-runbook includes kill switch and eviction policy (see bridge-ops-runbook.md).

Risks and mitigations:
- Noisy neighbor: Isolation knobs above reduce risk; in the event of cross-tenant degradation we will throttle Horizon first and notify Kimberly + Karthik.
- Cost overspend: We'll emit live cost burn metrics and cap burst count if burn rate passes the agreed threshold.

Request to Kimberly/Finance: confirm if Horizon prefers (A) flat-window pricing with an ex-ante credit, or (B) reserved + metered overage with a post-window reconciliation. If we go with (A) we can issue an invoice / credit letter that speeds procurement.

Attachments: bridge-ops-runbook.md (detailed rollback steps), sla-exemption-template.pdf

Marcus
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lim <sara@horizon-ai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity bridge for Horizon evaluation (2-week window)

Thanks everyone — this looks good and appreciated the operational detail. Two quick clarifications from our side:
- We prefer flat-window pricing (option A) to keep procurement simple. Can you send a short statement of work or invoice by EOD next Wednesday (2028-06-07)?
- For telemetry, can we get a read-only dashboard link that we can share with our engineering lead? If possible include the token burn tab and latency percentiles.

If those two are feasible we'll confirm the start window. Happy to sign the short term agreement (Procurement CC'ed).

Sara
Head of ML Platforms
Horizon AI
